issues.legal_issue: A retroactive definition of tenant does not extend rent-control protection to a pending eviction suit instituted under general property law when the premises were outside the earlier rent-control regime.
material_facts: The lease expired while the premises were excluded from the earlier rent-control statute, and the landlord then brought an eviction and mesne-profits suit under the Transfer of Property Act.

The later rent-control statute came into force while that suit was pending and included premises of this kind; its definition of tenant encompassed persons whose contractual tenancies had ended before the statute commenced.

The tenant remained in possession until after the eviction decree and the conclusion of the appeals, and the lower courts awarded mesne profits from the end of the lease until vacant possession was delivered.
issues.conclusion: The later statute did not govern the pending suit, which continued to be governed by the Transfer of Property Act. The tenant's occupation was therefore wrongful from the termination of the lease, and mesne profits were properly awarded from that point.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961, the definition of tenant is retroactive as to when the contractual tenancy ended, but it applies only where the Act governs the proceeding. Section 51(2) preserves pending proceedings under the repealed 1955 Act; it does not extend the 1961 Act to a pending suit brought under the Transfer of Property Act because the premises were exempt from the 1955 Act. Under section 111(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, the lease ended by efflux of time. Smt. Chander Kali Bai v. Shri Jagdish Singh Thakur was distinguished because the legal setting of that case did not involve a suit outside the earlier rent-control statute.

rule.if: appeal_from_mesne_profits_decree and pre_commencement_general_law_suit and premises_outside_prior_rent_regime and later_rent_law_does_not_extend_to_pending_general_law_suits

predicates.appeal_from_mesne_profits_decree: The occupant appealed a decree awarding mesne profits for continued possession after the lease ended.
predicates.pre_commencement_general_law_suit: The landlord filed the suit under general property law before the later rent-control law commenced.
predicates.premises_outside_prior_rent_regime: The premises were excluded from the rent-control regime in force when the suit was filed.
predicates.later_rent_law_does_not_extend_to_pendin: The later rent-control law did not provide that it governed pending suits brought under general property law.
predicates.post_termination_occupation_is_wrongful_: The occupant's possession after the lease ended is wrongful for purposes of awarding mesne profits.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns mesne profits in a pre-commencement general-law suit involving premises outside the prior rent-control regime, and the later law does not extend to pending general-law suits, occupation after the lease ends is wrongful for mesne profits.

issues.legal_issue: A concurrent assessment of damages based on evidence should not be reduced on appeal when no justifiable ground for disturbing it is shown.
material_facts: The trial court assessed monthly damages after considering the evidence, setting the rate below the landlord's claim but above the rent agreed in the lease.
The High Court reviewed the evidence and affirmed the trial court's rate.
The appellant challenged the rate on appeal, relying in part on the lower contractual rent, but the Supreme Court found no justifiable ground to reduce the concurrent assessment.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent assessment of damages was upheld, and the challenge to the rate was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the concurrent factual findings of the trial court and High Court on the evidence and found no justifiable basis for appellate interference. No separate statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.appeal_from_mesne_profits_assessment: The occupant appealed the rate of damages assessed in a mesne-profits proceeding.
predicates.concurrent_evidence_based_rate_findings: The trial court and the appellate court assessed the rate on the evidence and reached the same finding.
predicates.appellant_shows_no_justifiable_basis_for: The appellant challenged the assessed rate but did not establish a justifiable basis for reducing it.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a mesne-profits assessment based on evidence, the lower courts concur, and the appellant shows no justifiable basis for reduction, the concurrent rate is upheld.
